And then the key thing is then is to be able to find some availability in your calendars and book those meetings in with you.

Sometimes it runs over a little bit.
But these smaller businesses, they will sell with a due diligence period of about 30 days.

They will, which we again, you'll need a lawyer at that point.
But we'll, we'll again help sort of negotiate some points in there if it, it needs it.
The idea being really to get that signed off and for the deal to be closed and the money to be in your accounts within a sort of 30 to 60 day period after signing that LOI.

So it's a pretty tight ship that we run.
And the majority of time they do close within that period sometimes just to be sort of, you know, realistic, sometimes they can run over by a month or two.

So that's mainly strategic buyers.
Investment, sorry, equity funds, sorry, investment funds.

Yeah, you know, if they're looking for a bolt on, what they call a bolt on.
So that's when they're looking.
They've already bought the platform business and they're looking for smaller ones to bolt on.
But again, these transactions, the secondary ones tend to go through an agency and an agency founder is usually running that.
But we also deal with, I don't know if you've heard of SBA loans, but in the US they have a small business association and they guarantee these smaller loans.
So there's quite a few private buyers as well.
So for an example, you might find somebody that's left a larger agency and they don't want to start an agency from scratch.
They just want to buy one agency which they're then going to run themselves.
And they can get these guaranteed loans of up to about $5 million.
They're a little bit more than that now, but $5 million and they can buy a business and then run it themselves.

So there's either more strategic, where it's an agency group and they're looking to add on skill sets that they don't have, or you'll have a purely financial buyer which could be private equity back, but it could just be a group of private investors and.
Yeah, and private equity business as well.
So yeah, that's kind of the, the sort of general pool of buyers, if you like.
But we have all of those types of buyers in our network.
Obviously the agencies co platform attracts a lot of those SBA buyers as well.
Cool.
That makes Sense.

Is it something that, I mean, obviously negotiate it on a day to day, sorry, on a case by case level.
But is there any standard that you usually notice, any pattern, anything we can expect?
Yeah.

Between four and four and six times ebitda.
And what, what typically happens is you get half of that in cash up front and a three year earn out or seller finance, however you want, want to look at how that's made up.
Now that is kind of like the average place that deals on, but every single deal is different.
You know, it really does depend on the circumstances of every buyer and seller, you know, because there's always a point to negotiate.
But also it's very much about the story that we go to the market with.
You know, if the real story is Alessia, that you're not in the business, then we will go to market with that.
You know, you're out of the business already and you're playing an investor role in the company and you're not really involved.

You know, we go to market with that story and it just is the, the deal that we're trying to get.
So most buyers want the founders to stay in, unless they're these SBA buyers who again, they would prefer to get everybody out and run it themselves.
So it really does, it really does depend.

But you know, the best thing for us to do is to go to the market and get as many different types of buyers to the table as possible and give you a bunch of options and we can decide, you know, then it might be that we find a really great large agency that Francesco wants to stay in the business for three and maybe like staying forever.
You know, it could be a really good opportunity for him.

Awesome, awesome.
Perfect.

Sounds perfect.

Yeah, so.

We talked USD dollars.
Yeah.

Okay, that's perfect.

Correct?

On the commission at the end of it.
So that's.

It's on the cash up front plus.
The seller and the earn out.

But yeah, we don't take it until you've had the payment for each thing.

Francesco for sure will have a few more questions as well.

Is about correct.

Perfect.

Sounds perfect.
Awesome.
Andy, thank you very much for your time.
Really appreciate it.
Yeah, my pleasure meet you both.
Yeah, thanks a lot.

summary.overview: In a recent Business Development and M&A consultation meeting, Alessio Cordeddu and Francesco from 99ads discussed their company's readiness for potential sale with Andy Day from Capital A Group, an M&A advisory focused on marketing services. The meeting centered around 99ads’ business model, which targets e-commerce stores with significant advertising budgets, primarily on platforms like Meta and TikTok, and projected an EBITDA of $800,000 by year-end, indicating an opportune moment for exit. Andy detailed Capital A's M&A process, including a $30,000 advisory fee, a 5% commission on the deal's total value, and a recommended timeline for initiating the sale in May or June to achieve closure by late fall. Key action items included Alessio reaching out to Andy to initiate the formal M&A process and both partners preparing the company for a smooth transition, which involves training a replacement for Francesco's role.
summary.short_summary: In a recent consultation, Alessio Cordeddu and Francesco from 99ads met with Andy Day from Capital A Group to evaluate the company's readiness for a potential sale. The discussion covered 99ads' business model, which targets e-commerce stores with significant advertising budgets, primarily on Meta, with a projected EBITDA of $800,000 by year-end, suggesting a favorable exit opportunity. Andy detailed Capital A's M&A process, which includes a $30,000 advisory fee and a 5% commission on the deal's total value. He recommended starting the sale process in May or June to achieve closure by late fall. Key action items included Alessio reaching out to Andy to initiate the M&A process and the partners preparing the company for a smooth transition, including training a replacement for Francesco.
